::: callout-note
## Overview

This module introduces students to a rotation-based research workflow designed to highlight reproducibility, uncertainty, and analytical decision-making. Students work with shared data, rotate roles within research teams, and reflect on how analytic choices affect results. The project emphasizes transparent documentation and iterative improvement. By the end of the module, students will have produced a reproducible analysis and reflected on research practices.
:::

::: callout-success
## Motivation and Learning Goals

- Understand how analytic decisions shape research findings  
- Practice reproducible data analysis and documentation  
- Develop skills in collaborative and rotating research roles  
:::

::: callout-warning
## Context for Use

This module is designed for upper-division undergraduate courses and works well in methods, data analysis, or research design classes. It can be implemented in in-person, hybrid, or online formats. Estimated time commitment is **5–6 class periods**.
:::

## Prerequisites

Students should have prior exposure to basic data analysis concepts and familiarity with either R or Python. They should also be comfortable interpreting summary statistics and simple visualizations.

## Implementation

### Guide to Included Materials {#materials}

| Type | File/Link | Description |
|-------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Instructor Handout | `files/instructor-handout.pdf` | Notes for pacing and assessment |
| Student Worksheet | `files/student-worksheet.qmd` | Steps and prompts for students |
| Slides (optional) | `files/slides.pdf` | Overview figures and key questions |
| Dataset A | `data/dataset-a.csv` | Raw measurements |
| Dataset B | `data/dataset-b.csv` | Cleaned subset |

### Practical Tips {#tips}

Provide clear expectations for role rotation and documentation early in the project. Anticipate common misconceptions about uncertainty and replication. Consider accessibility needs and provide alternative formats where appropriate.

## Assessment {#assessment}

- **Formative:** clicker questions, think-pair-share prompts, checkpoint plots  
- **Summative:** rubric for final figure plus a 300-word memo assessing analytic decisions  
- **Answer keys / exemplars:** stored with instructor materials

## Variations and Extensions {#variations}

### Level Variations

This module can be simplified by reducing the number of analytic choices or expanded by incorporating additional datasets or modeling techniques.

### Follow-ups and Links to Other Work

Learning outcomes can be reinforced through later assignments focused on replication, robustness checks, or peer review of analyses.
